newsitem.title: CHINA: China's grain, oil prices decline in May.
newsitem.headline: China's grain, oil prices decline in May.

text.p: China's grain and edible oil prices declined in May from the previous month because of oversupply, the Economic Daily said on Friday.
The average national wheat price stood at 1,608 yuan ($193.7) per tonne in May, down from 1,687 yuan in April, the newspaper quoted figures released by the Zhengzhou Commodity Exchange as saying.
Wheat pices continued to fall because supply had already exceeded demand, it said.
The average national corn price stood at 1,081 yuan per tonne, down from 1,107 yuan in April, it said. Corn prices remained sluggish.
Corn prices were expected to fluctuate at relatively low levels in the rest of 1997 bacause of rising output and falling demand by the depressed feed industry, it said.
China's average national price of long-grain rice was 1,914 yuan in May, down by 4.6 percent from April, it said. Price of round-grain rice was 2,165 yuan, down by 6.0 percent, it said.

The average price of peanut oil was 9,867 yuan per tonne, down by 1.3 percent from April, rapeseed oil at 7,486 yuan per tonne, down by 0.5 percent and soybean oil at 7,404 yuan, down by 1.6 percent, it said.
